papers.abstract: The blind perspective-$n$-point (PnP) problem is to estimate the pose of a calibrated camera from 2D and 3D point sets with unknown correspondences. We show that, for complete, noiseless observations, fourteen permutation-invariant image moments up to order four identify a fixed camera pose for almost every 3D point set containing at least twenty points. Our learning-free method, MomentPnP, matches these moments between the observed 2D points and the projected 3D points to initialize a camera pose without correspondences and refines the pose and correspondence weights using expectation--maximization. Across the test sets of three benchmarks, our method reduces median rotation error by $5$--$170\times$ relative to the best learned baseline, both with and without outliers. We recover accurate poses even with as many outliers as inliers. On dense ETH3D scans, pose accuracy improves as the point sets grow, even as individual correspondences become harder to resolve.

papers.title: VA-Assembly: View-Aligned Score Guidance for Training-Free 3D Part Assembly
papers.authors: Yeon-Jae Kim; Sangwon Kang; Byung-Kwon Min
papers.abstract: Image-to-3D foundation models have improved 3D reconstruction, but typically produce monolithic representations without explicit part-level structure. Part-aware generation and learning-based assembly methods often require part-level supervision, category-specific priors, or paired part-layout training data. We instead consider a practical but underexplored setting in which independently prepared or generated 3D parts have no predefined inter-part relationships, shared coordinate frames, or consistent scales, and must be assembled into a reference-consistent object from a single image. We present VA-Assembly, a training-free framework for 3D part assembly through part-level transformation estimation using view-aligned diffusion guidance. Given a reference image and fixed 3D part geometries, VA-Assembly optimizes each part's translation, rotation, and scale. We condition a frozen view-conditioned diffusion model on same-view renderings of a reference-derived monolithic 3D representation, producing score gradients geometrically aligned with the part configuration. This guidance provides multi-view structural cues under large initial misalignment. By repurposing pretrained visual-structural priors as transformation-level supervision, VA-Assembly requires no annotated part layouts, predefined part taxonomies, category-specific assembly training, or bounding-box-based layout initialization. Experiments compare VA-Assembly with geometric registration and compositional layout baselines using each baseline's supported transformation components, showing improved part-wise transformation estimation. Ablation studies show that view-aligned conditioning, rather than diffusion guidance alone, is critical for reliable transformation gradients. Updating only part transformations preserves explicit component separability and supports component-level editing, replacement, and reconfiguration.

papers.title: UNITE: Consolidating Embodied VLM Specialists via Shared-Anchor One-Bit Factorization
papers.authors: Tao Tao; Anke Tang; Enneng Yang; Zhi Hou; Xiaogang Wang et al.
papers.abstract: Embodied capabilities such as visual grounding, spatial reasoning, navigation, and driving understanding are often developed in separate vision-language specialists fine-tuned from a common pretrained model.Deploying the specialists separately multiplies storage, whereas merging them into one dense model forces conflicting task updates to share parameters and loses part of each specialist's expertise.We introduce UNITE, a framework that consolidates such specialists into a compact shared-backbone mixture of experts. UNITE keeps the feed-forward block of each specialist as a routable expert and represents the expert bank through a shared-anchor one-bit factorization: a shared floating-point anchor plus expert-specific, row-scaled binary deviations.The anchor is optimized jointly with the scales and signs through closed-form alternating updates, using only source weights and no calibration data.Router adaptation then adjusts token-level expert selection with the backbone and experts frozen, updating fewer than $0.6$M parameters ($<0.01\%$ of the $8.8$B active parameters). Built from four Qwen3-VL-8B specialists, the complete UNITE model occupies $20.3$ GB, $1.16\times$ the storage of one dense specialist and $59.6\%$ below the uncompressed MoE. Across $22$ benchmarks and R2R Val-Unseen, UNITE matches six static merging methods in mean retention of best-specialist performance, leads all of them on Scan2Cap, ScanQA, and all four navigation metrics, and surpasses every source specialist on all five 3D scene understanding benchmarks (up to $+19.1$ on Scan2Cap) and on R2R navigation. Relative to the uncompressed MoE, factorization is nearly lossless on $21$ of $22$ benchmarks; the exception is VSI-Bench, where frame-count experiments suggest impaired use of cross-frame evidence.UNITE thus consolidates complementary embodied capabilities near single-model storage.

papers.title: Rigidity and classification of complete translating solitons and self-expanders with constant curvature in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$
papers.authors: Zhi Li; Cheng Xing
papers.abstract: For complete immersed surfaces in Euclidean four-space whose mean curvature vector has constant length, translators are affine planes parallel to their fixed nonzero velocity, and self-expanders are planes through their centre. This rigidity requires no Lagrangian assumption, properness, volume growth control, or bound on the second fundamental form. Complete Lagrangian translators and self-expanders in $\mathbb{C}^{2}$ with constant Gaussian curvature are flat and, up to unitary equivalence, are properly embedded products of two complete planar curves. Translating factors are lines or grim reapers. Expanding factors are lines through the origin or nonstraight self-expanders. The proofs use moving frames, a transnormal function, a cubic tensor identity, and analytic continuation.

papers.title: Directionality of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO experiment
papers.authors: F. D. Amaro; E. Baracchini; L. Benussi; C. Capoccia; M. Caponero et al.
papers.abstract: Electron-recoil directionality can help distinguish solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds and, together with recoil-energy measurements and three-dimensional tracking, enable neutrino-energy spectroscopy. We study the reconstruction of the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO optical time-projection chamber, focusing on the 50 L LIME prototype and its high-granularity scientific CMOS (sCMOS) readout. A dedicated algorithm identifies the interaction point from the asymmetry of the track light distribution and estimates the recoil direction from the early portion of the ionization trail, before multiple scattering erases most of the directional information. The method is characterized with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of electron recoils and detector response. Samples spanning 15 keV to 70 keV are used to optimize the algorithm parameters by minimizing the width of the reconstructed-minus-true projected-angle distribution. The projected angular response is modeled by two Gaussian components that account for its dependence on track inclination. The narrower component, associated with favorable projections approximately parallel to the Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) plane, has a width that improves from about $20^\circ$ near 20 keV to about $12^\circ$ at 60 keV. We also quantify the fraction of events in the correctly reconstructed angular core and discuss the dominant limitations of a camera-only two-dimensional measurement.

papers.title: European derivatives pricing via constrained Gaussian process regressions
papers.authors: Arnaud Servais; Donatien Hainaut
papers.abstract: This article develops a Gaussian process method for pricing European derivatives when the underlyings, and the risk factors driving them, follow a multivariate jump-diffusion. A Gaussian process prior on the pricing function is conditioned on the Feynman-Kac partial integro-differential equation at a set of collocation points. The price is returned as a closed-form and differentiable function, allowing the Greeks to be obtained without simulation or finite differences. The jump terms are handled iteratively: the price is computed as the limit of a sequence of boundary value problems. Our main theoretical contribution is a convergence result for this iteration: using Weissinger's fixed-point theorem in the supremum norm, we show that it converges from any starting point, and provide a worst-case number of iterations for a given precision. The method is illustrated with derivatives of two underlyings under the Heston model with Kou double-exponential jumps, a five-dimensional problem, and benchmarked against Monte Carlo simulation.

papers.title: A Seismic Foundation Model for Dense Feature Extraction
papers.authors: Zhixiang Guo; Xinming Wu; Yimin Dou; Hui Gao; Siyao Zhao et al.
papers.abstract: Deep-learning-based seismic interpretation is constrained by scarce high-quality annotations, and most existing models are trained separately for individual tasks. We present SeisDFE, a 7B-parameter seismic foundation model for dense feature extraction, pretrained on 5.34 million 2D images derived from more than 500 seismic volumes. A three-stage pretraining strategy, combining discriminative self-supervised learning, Gram feature anchoring, and multi-resolution adaptation, improves feature discriminability while preserving spatial coherence. With its encoder frozen, SeisDFE supports seismic facies classification, salt detection, fault detection, and relative geologic time estimation. It outperforms existing seismic foundation models on all four tasks and a natural-image-pretrained model on all but fault detection, with the largest gains under scarce supervision: using only two annotated sections of the F3 dataset, it improves whole-volume mIoU by 12-19 percentage points over the baselines. The learned features remain effective with task-specific decoders and extend to synthetic-to-field transfer and sparse 3D geobody interpretation. These results show that large-scale seismic pretraining organizes geological information into dense representations that are directly reusable across interpretation tasks.

papers.title: An adaptive Gaussian splitting scheme for linear Fokker--Planck equations
papers.authors: Markus Bachmayr; Tianyu Jin; Damiano Lombardi; Olga Mula; Ahmad Zorkot
papers.abstract: We develop an adaptive numerical method for linear Fokker--Planck equations on $\mathbb R^d$, based on approximating the evolving probability density by linear combinations of Gaussian functions (LCGs). The method applies to polynomial-type drift fields, without requiring a gradient-flow structure or a stationary distribution. It relies on an operator splitting that separates diffusion and affine drift, for which Gaussian functions can be propagated exactly, from higher-order transport, whose evolution is approximated adaptively by LCGs. Both the number of Gaussian components and their means and covariances are adjusted to meet the prescribed accuracy tolerances. The adaptivity is driven by computable error indicators involving polynomial moments of Gaussians that can be evaluated analytically. We provide a rigorous error analysis that relates the approximation error to the indicators driving adaptivity and illustrate the performance of the scheme in several test cases.

papers.title: CLIFT: Contrastive LiDAR Instance Features for 3D Pedestrian Tracking
papers.authors: German Devchich; Timur Akhtyamov; Denis Fatykhoph; Gonzalo Ferrer
papers.abstract: A social robot has to keep track of the people around it over time to plan its motion, a task handled by 3D multi-object tracking. For the LiDAR modality, trackers usually sit on top of a detector and link its detections across frames with a separate motion model or re-identification network. We instead show how a 3D LiDAR detector itself can be turned into a tracker by adding an instance-level contrastive objective on its intermediate voxel features. Each embedding is read from the voxels inside a detected box, and boxes are matched across frames by cosine similarity and the Hungarian algorithm, without a motion model. The detector backbone is fine-tuned together with this objective, which learns identity-aware features while leaving detection accuracy essen- tially intact. Because the method uses only the voxel features that Li- DAR detectors already produce, it is backbone-agnostic. On the JRDB 3D tracking leaderboard our LiDAR-only tracker ranks first on HOTA (38.58) and IDF1 (37.99), 13.04 and 9.30 points above the next pub- lished method, and second on MOTA and OSPA. Code is available at https://hermak56.github.io/CLIFT/.

papers.title: State-Dependent Saving and Heavy-Tailed Shocks in a Stochastic Solow Growth Model via a Logistic Lévy Framework
papers.authors: Wen Wang; Shenglan Yuan
papers.abstract: This work develops a stochastic Solow growth model in which the aggregate saving rate is state dependent and evolves on a faster time scale than capital. The saving target follows a mean-reverting process driven by symmetric $α$-stable Lévy noise, while the saving control adjusts toward this target and capital accumulates according to a Solow equation. After scaling, the model is a three-dimensional stochastic dynamical system with multiplicative heavy-tailed noise and a logistic saving function. We establish invariance of the economically meaningful state space for the discrete reflected model, derive the stationary distribution of the saving target in the Gaussian limiting case, and characterize how the tail index and logistic sensitivity affect the coupled dynamics. Monte Carlo simulations show bimodal capital and saving distributions, asymmetric first-passage behavior between low- and high-capital regimes, and a nonlinear relationship between output volatility, the logistic sensitivity, and the tail index. In particular, heavier tails increase the dispersion of the scaled saving target and low-to-high first-passage frequencies, but do not necessarily increase relative output volatility. The results highlight the importance of state-dependent saving and non-Gaussian shocks for growth dynamics.

papers.title: Efficient Multi-View Generation with Iterative Global-Local Proxy Attention
papers.authors: Wei Tan; Kunming Luo; Hongyu Yan; Yu Zhang; Zihao Zhang et al.
papers.abstract: Generating consistent multi-view RGB images and normal maps from a single input image provides complementary appearance and geometric cues for 3D reconstruction. However, maintaining cross-view consistency requires information exchange across viewpoints, and dense cross-view attention becomes computationally expensive as the number of views and spatial resolution increase. In this paper, we propose Global-Local Proxy Attention (GLPA) to reduce cross-view communication costs while preserving fine-grained within-view processing. Specifically, GLPA retains full-resolution interactions within each view and uses compact global proxies for cross-view communication. To further leverage the exchanged information, GLPA incorporates iterative proxy refinement, which rebuilds the proxies from updated features and reuses the same attention parameters for subsequent interactions within a single denoising step. We evaluate GLPA on two structurally different diffusion backbones, FLUX and Stable Diffusion. Experiments on FLUX show that GLPA achieves a $2.65\times$ speedup in attention computation per denoising step over dense attention, while improving reconstruction IoU from 0.6849 to 0.7019 and reducing NVS LPIPS from 0.086 to 0.076. Results on Stable Diffusion further demonstrate the effectiveness of GLPA, with a $1.80\times$ attention speedup and improvements across all five quality metrics.

papers.title: SpeCal: Spectral Calibration for Unsupervised RLVR
papers.authors: Kai Tang; Xing Zheng; Haobo Wang; Guangcheng Zhu; Shenzhi Yang et al.
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved the reasoning abilities of large language models, but its dependence on ground-truth answers or external verifiers limits its ability to exploit abundant unlabeled reasoning data. Unsupervised RLVR alleviates this bottleneck by deriving scalar rewards from the model's own rollouts. However, the reliability of such self-generated supervision varies substantially across rollout groups and individual responses, while existing methods construct or refine their rewards mainly from decoded outcomes and reward statistics. These endpoint signals reveal what answers the model produces, but provide limited information about whether the underlying rollout representations form a reliable structure for learning. Our key observation is that hidden-state spectra offer a complementary view of supervision reliability by characterizing both the organization of a rollout group and the support received by each rollout within that group. Based on this observation, we propose SpeCal, a bi-level spectral calibration framework for unsupervised RLVR. At the group level, SpeCal combines spectral mass with a Gaussian band-pass gate over normalized entropy-based effective rank, favoring rollout groups with substantial representation variation whose effective dimensionality lies in a preferred regime. At the rollout level, the same group effective rank determines how many dominant directions are retained in a leave-one-out spectral subspace formed by the remaining rollouts, within which the conditional support of each held-out rollout is measured. The resulting signals calibrate the original reward-induced advantages at the group and rollout levels without redefining the underlying unlabeled reward.

papers.title: Bayesian variable selection via collapsed importance-weighted variational inference over discrete model spaces
papers.authors: Mai Mai; Matias Quiroz; Minh-Ngoc Tran
papers.abstract: Bayesian variable selection under spike-and-slab priors provides interpretable posterior inclusion probabilities for individual predictors, but exploring large discrete model spaces using conventional Markov chain Monte Carlo methods can be computationally challenging. We develop a collapsed importance-weighted variational framework for Gaussian linear regression. The framework analytically integrates out the remaining model parameters and directly approximates the posterior over binary inclusion indicators using a factorised Bernoulli distribution. To improve posterior inclusion probability estimation while retaining the computational simplicity of the factorised variational family, we replace the conventional evidence lower bound with a tighter variational Rényi importance-weighted lower bound. We establish a finite-sample upper bound on posterior inclusion probability approximation errors and show that, under suitable conditions, the optimised variational inclusion probabilities converge to their exact posterior counterparts as the number of importance samples increases and the Rényi parameter decreases appropriately. We further establish that analytical marginalisation tightens the variational objective and the corresponding inclusion probability error bound, while reducing importance-weight variance and improving the asymptotic efficiency of importance-sampling post-processing. To address the challenges of estimating gradients with respect to the variational parameters when the inclusion indicators are discrete, we leverage recent advances in variance-reduced score-function estimators, together with an annealing strategy to stabilise optimisation. Simulation experiments and empirical applications demonstrate improvements in posterior inclusion probability estimation relative to standard variational inference and two existing variational approaches.

papers.title: Near-synchronous multiphoton quantum interference
papers.authors: Xiangshuai Dong; Tingzeng Wu
papers.abstract: Nonclassical multiphoton interference is an important resource for optical quantum information processing, and its output statistics depend on the distinguishability of the input photons. In this paper, using time delay as a tunable parameter, we theoretically analyze the interference behavior of independent pure-state single photons with identical Gaussian spectral envelopes under near-synchronous conditions. Using the immanant representation of the single-photon internal-state overlap matrix to express the weights of the exchange-symmetry components, we determine the leading asymptotic behavior and approximation error of each weight, and characterize the weight suppression laws when different groups of photons become synchronized on different scales. Given the local identity classes of the delay functions and the vanishing orders of pairwise delay differences, the vanishing orders of the weights of the exchange-symmetry components can be computed in polynomial time by integer minimum-cost flow. On this basis, we provide a network-independent total-variation error bound for the complete output photon-number distribution, establish a quantitative relationship among the photon spectral width, synchronization precision, and interference statistics deviation, and provide a quantitative basis for the analysis and approximation of near-synchronous multiphoton interference.

papers.title: SiGMA: Site-Grounded Multi-Modal ISAC Data Generation for Environment-Aware Communications
papers.authors: Yijie Bian; Wei Guo; Kai Zhang; Xiao Ye; Shurui Xu et al.
papers.abstract: Learning-based multi-modal integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) requires data that associate environmental observations with the wireless response generated by the same site and dynamic scene state. Acquiring such data at new sites requires sensor calibration, coordinated measurements, and cross-modal association. We present site-grounded multi-modal ISAC data generation (SiGMA), which combines OpenStreetMap (OSM), Overture Maps, and procedural three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction to create georeferenced urban scenes. A shared scene geometry and time-indexed actor state link synchronized red-green-blue (RGB) images, light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point clouds, positioning records, frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) Radar in-phase and quadrature (IQ) samples, and ray-traced wireless channels. For configurable reflected propagation under direct-link blockage, SiGMA generates optional reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) component channels for phase-configuration evaluation across shared scene states. The evaluation results demonstrate that the framework improves zero-shot beam prediction performance on real DeepSense 6G measurements compared with an OSM-derived synthetic-data baseline. A camera-assisted RIS case study further demonstrates the generation of sensing-associated supervision for configurable reflected propagation. The dataset generation pipeline is available at https://github.com/Trans-cending/SiGMA-main.

papers.title: Explicit topology control in isogeometric topology optimization using persistent homology
papers.authors: Wenliang Yin; Gengchen Li; Hongwei Lin
papers.abstract: Explicitly controlling structural topology remains a major challenge in topology optimization. While many implicit methods regulate topology only indirectly, available explicit strategies often focus on two-dimensional hole control or extend to 3D without a unified treatment of tunnels and cavities. This study proposes a differentiable, persistent homology-based framework for explicit topology control in 2D and 3D isogeometric topology optimization. A NURBS-represented density field induces a single sublevel filtration whose persistence diagrams quantify the connected components, holes in 2D, and tunnels and cavities in 3D directly. To enforce prescribed bounds on topological feature counts, weighted topological objectives are applied in a staged manner that coordinates the different homology dimensions. Each redundant feature is removed either by cutting or by filling according to the region of its corresponding persistence pair, avoiding the excessive structural changes associated with filling alone. The topological inverse mapping yields analytical sensitivities with respect to the density control coefficients, so that the resulting objective is readily incorporated into gradient-based optimization and solved by the method of moving asymptotes. Numerical experiments on 2D and 3D benchmarks demonstrate explicit and reliable topology control while maintaining competitive mechanical performance and stable convergence.

papers.title: Universality of Brown measure convergence for non-Gaussian matrix polynomials with adjoints
papers.authors: Yi Han
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a noncommutative polynomial of arbitrary degree. We prove that the empirical spectral distribution of $P$ evaluated at independent Wigner matrices converges weakly in probability to its Brown measure limit. The same conclusion holds for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent iid matrices and their adjoints. The entry laws have bounded real or joint planar densities and a finite $(2+\varepsilon)$ moment; only second moments are required on the Wigner diagonal. The real and imaginary parts of an entry may be dependent, and its pseudovariance need not vanish. The proof develops the coefficient-algebra approach of the author's earlier work on matrix polynomials with Gaussian and non-Gaussian iid inputs \cite{Han}. The main step is a polynomial lower-tail estimate, under only second moments, for the least singular value of a tensor pencil with arbitrary fixed matrix coefficients. We use a logarithmic determinant method: a real-block small-ball argument shows that logarithmic derivatives of the determinant control the inverse pencil. Relative polynomial anti-concentration then gives the lower-tail bound. We establish convergence of logarithmic potentials by Hermitian resolvent comparison and rank truncation. This extends the recent Brown measure convergence theorem of Collins, Kitagawa, Miyagawa, Yuan and Zhong \cite{Collins} for GUE polynomials to non-Gaussian Wigner inputs.

papers.title: When is Uniform Sampling Optimal? Coresets for Distributional Clustering
papers.authors: Junqiu Hu; Lingxiao Huang; Baoduo Xu
papers.abstract: Recent work [1] settled the optimal worst-case strong $\varepsilon$-coreset size for Euclidean $k$-means in unrestricted dimension at $\tildeΘ(\min\{k^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-2}, k\varepsilon^{-4}\})$, showing that the natural target $\tilde{O}(k\varepsilon^{-2})$ is unattainable in general. For mixtures of $k$ isotropic Gaussian components with balanced weights and bounded scale imbalance in dimension $d\ge\log k$, we show that uniform sampling yields strong $\varepsilon$-coresets of size $\tilde{O}(k\varepsilon^{-2})$, without cluster separation. This saves a factor of $\min\{\sqrt{k},\varepsilon^{-2}\}$ over the worst-case bound, up to logarithms. For population approximation by independent, equally weighted samples, the near-linear rate is optimal up to logarithmic factors over this class.   More generally, for datasets generated from an isotropic Gaussian mixture $μ$ satisfying a mild cost-comparison assumption, uniform sampling yields strong $\varepsilon$-coresets of size $\tilde{O}((kζ_μ+π_{\min}^{-1})\varepsilon^{-2})$, where $π_{\min}$ is the minimum component weight and $ζ_μ$ measures scale imbalance. Our proof uses a base-shift cost decomposition: one query center per component describes the base costs, and graph spanners control the sparse corrections from points switching centers. For general mixtures under cost and tail assumptions, we obtain $\tilde{O}((kζ_μ+π_{\min}^{-1})\varepsilon^{-2}\min\{\sqrt{k},\varepsilon^{-2}\})$ samples. We also prove a matching $\tildeΩ(\min\{k^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-2},k\varepsilon^{-4}\})$ lower bound for population approximation by uniform sampling from anisotropic Gaussian mixtures, even with equal weights and a shared covariance matrix.   [1] Junqiu Hu, Lingxiao Huang, Jian Li, and Baoduo Xu. Tight coreset bounds for $(k, z)$-clustering in Euclidean and doubling metrics, 2026. arXiv:2610.34373.

papers.title: From Joint Risk to Decision Invariance: Decision-Preserving Regularization for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning
papers.authors: Qi Zhu; Ziang Gan; Wanting Zhang; Libao Zhang
papers.abstract: Exemplar-free continual learning seeks to minimize joint risk over all seen tasks, yet historical data are unavailable for direct optimization. We observe that, for classification, preserving the model's decisions on previously learned classes helps retain old knowledge. This motivates Decision-Preserving Regularization (DPR). Penalizing changes in all pairwise old-class logit margins reduces algebraically to a centered relative-logit penalty. We further apply spectral whitening to remove the classifier's spectral scale bias. Because the global classifier supplies the decision constraints for the next stage, it must remain calibrated across all seen classes despite the drift of stored old-class statistics during representation updates. We therefore fit a closed-form affine map from paired current-task features to transport old-class Gaussian means and covariances into the updated feature space, then calibrate the global classifier using these distributions and current-task features. Across CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, ImageNet-Subset, and ImageNet-1K under cold-start protocols, comparisons with state-of-the-art methods show that DPR achieves higher accuracy in most settings while remaining highly efficient. Code is available at https://github.com/bnufw/dpr.

papers.title: GPRidge: Gaussian-process Accelerated Calculations of Minimum Energy Paths and First-order Saddle Points
papers.authors: Rohit Goswami; Maxim Masterov; Satish Kamath; Alejandro Pena-Torres; Andreas Lynge Vishart et al.
papers.abstract: GPRidge, a Gaussian-process (GP) library for accelerating calculations of minimum energy paths and first-order saddle points with compiled-language and Python bindings, is presented. An evaluation controller uses GP predictions to iteratively adjust the Cartesian coordinates of the atoms. The fitted GP energy surface and measured energies and forces pass from the path calculation to local refinement of the saddle point. New evaluations improve the surrogate and check the candidate geometry. For the molecular calculations, acceptance requires measured-force convergence and an independent Hessian with only one negative eigenvalue. A second negative eigenvalue triggers an escape and renewed refinement. The controller supports a joint inverse-distance GP for molecules and local GP residuals on periodic systems. Applications to the 24 Baker-Chan and 20 Birkholz-Schlegel molecular reactions using the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA-S-1.1), and to 72 Pt heptamer and island rearrangements on Pt(111) using a Morse potential, are presented. On matched Baker-Chan reactions, GPRidge uses 7.8- and 7.0-fold fewer energy-and-force evaluations than climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) and off-path climbing-image nudged elastic band (OCI-NEB), respectively, reducing validation-inclusive CI-NEB time by 41%. All 20 Birkholz-Schlegel saddle points pass the independent index-one check, compared with 17 for the classical dimer method started from the same path maxima; on those 17 reactions, the GP dimer stage uses 6.4-fold fewer evaluations. All 72 Pt(111) paths meet the OptBench force criterion, with median evaluation counts of 30 and 23 for the heptamer and island problems, against 778 and 443 for CI-NEB.

papers.title: multiCAsp: Spatially Informed Canonical Association Analysis of Multi-Omic Data
papers.authors: Ziqi Mu; Qiuyi Wu; Zhicheng Ji; Pixu Shi
papers.abstract: Simultaneous profiling of multiple molecular layers at spatially resolved locations creates opportunities to identify shared cross-modal biological variation in its tissue context. We present multiCAsp (multi-omic Canonical Association informed by spatial graph), a probabilistic latent-factor model for integrating $M \geq 2$ spatially resolved omic modalities. It incorporates spatial dependence through a graph-Laplacian prior on shared latent factors and uses an expectation-maximization algorithm to estimate factor scores and modality-specific feature loadings. Because the prior is defined on a neighborhood graph rather than on Euclidean distances, it accommodates irregular tissue geometries and extends naturally to multiple tissue sections. Simulations show that multiCAsp consistently achieves higher mean latent subspace and loading recovery than alternative methods across varying sample sizes, feature dimensions, and noise levels, with the largest gains under high noise. Compared with an existing Gaussian process-based spatial factor model, it is also less sensitive to how the spatial coordinates are represented, produces spatially smoother factors, and has lower computational cost. Applied to metabolomic-proteomic data from macaque cortex and gene-protein data from human renal carcinoma, multiCAsp recovers spatially coherent multi-omic factors with interpretable biological signatures. In the macaque data, transferred factors retain broad spatial patterns across animals and support cross-modal prediction of protein abundances from metabolomic measurements.

papers.title: Nonsense rank correlations between independent random walks
papers.authors: Zhongming Xie; Liping Zhu
papers.abstract: Yule's nonsense correlation persists for Spearman's rho and Kendall's tau between independent random walks. Neither coefficient concentrates at zero as the sample size grows. For centred random walks with finite increment variances, we derive a universal joint limit expressed through Brownian occupation functionals. Integral formulas give limiting variances of approximately 0.222 and 0.108, respectively, below the Pearson value of 0.241. Rank correlations thus reduce the limiting dispersion on their respective coefficient scales. We prove that both marginal limits have symmetric densities and represent them exactly as limits of polynomial densities determined by Gaussian moment integrals. Spearman's conventional t test and Kendall's normal approximation are asymptotically invalid, with rejection probabilities tending to one under process independence.

papers.title: OrthoMark: Place Recognition with Point-Anchored Orthographic Height Mark
papers.authors: Haichuan Li
papers.abstract: LiDAR place recognition provides the loop closures of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping(SLAM). Perspective from Z-axis, a gravity-aligned scan is an orthographic map of the scene, and a revisit from another position and heading moves this map rigidly in the plane, a motion that a polar Fourier spectrum ignores and phase correlation recovers. Along the vertical, the heights of the returns describe the structures, but which heights are observed depends on the range, because the sensor's vertical field of view cuts nearby structures low; height thus misleads a global key, yet is decisive once two scans are aligned and compared cell by cell where they overlap. We present \method, a training-free method built on one principle: two LiDAR scans can only be compared through features computed from the same geometric surfaces in both scans. \method retrieves candidates with a translation- and rotation-invariant polar spectrum of the bird's-eye view (BEV), 1.9,KB per keyframe, and verifies each candidate by estimating its planar pose through phase correlation and scoring it with \emph{point-anchored height columns}: every BEV cell keeps a 16-bit mask of the heights of its own returns; within a session, the score is weighted by the expected overlap of the two scans' sensing ranges, computed from their distance. We show that this vertical link pays off in verification but hurts in retrieval, where what a height slice contains depends on the range to the structure. For single robot, \method has the highest AP of the training-free methods without 3D registration on the KITTI development sequences; across robots, on all multi-robot sequences, it matches or exceeds RING++ at 1/350 of its descriptor size and closes more inter-robot loops than the learned BEVPlace++ on all tests.

papers.title: Calibrated Functional Prediction from Overlapping Nonlinear Observations
papers.authors: Peida Li
papers.abstract: We study prediction of nonlinear audit functionals from scalar observations of a shared hidden table state. For Schur-rational operators, local Gaussian projections yield a common sparse kernel for overlapping tasks, repeated row identities, and cross-row dependence. Shared-state residual samples extend this kernel through a positive-semidefinite feature representation. Positive matrix integration and sample-value enclosures connect the original inputs to the actual saved hybrid prediction. A sorted calibration-role perturbation bound then certifies its complete finite-pool pinball risk. Independent complete-loss selection chooses the ridge, score scale, and residual weight, while task-rank calibration supplies an upper endpoint. Evaluation uses twenty new reference contexts per dataset at two task sizes, giving 400 conditions across ten benchmark populations. The mean dataset complete-loss ratios are 0.9977 to the degree-two kernel, 0.9961 to matched complete-MC shrinkage, and 0.9911 to the retrospective minimum over 174 public configurations. The last ratio has a paired reference-bootstrap interval of [0.9898,0.9927]. On 40 profiles at coefficient tolerance $10^{-7}$, Gamma quadrature has a geometric mean cold-time ratio of .0646 to strengthened Arb/Petras integration.

papers.title: Vision-Language Grounded Semantic Navigation for Autonomous Mobile Robots
papers.authors: Ravindran Vasoor Saravanan; Chittin Varunav Ravi; Madhumita Singh; Thirulok Sundar Mohan Rasu
papers.abstract: Language-guided navigation enables mobile robots to interpret natural language commands and navigate toward user-specified targets in unstructured environments. However, integrating open-vocabulary visual perception with classical robotics pipelines for mapping and navigation remains a challenging problem. In this work, we present a complete ROS2-based system that combines frontier-based exploration, open-vocabulary object detection using Grounding DINO, depth-based 3D localization, and semantic mapping to enable end-to-end vision-language grounded navigation in simulation. The system accepts natural language commands such as ``go to the yellow box,'' detects candidate objects from RGB images using text prompts, estimates their positions in the world frame, and generates navigation goals executed by the Nav2 stack. In a Gazebo-based indoor environment with a TurtleBot3 robot, the system autonomously explored the room, detected three of the five target objects, and successfully executed both natural language navigation commands tested, without task-specific training. The results indicate that open-vocabulary grounding models can be integrated into classical navigation pipelines, though performance is limited by detection uncertainty, depth-based localization error, and incomplete exploration coverage. These findings highlight both the feasibility and current limitations of deploying vision-language grounded navigation systems using lightweight, CPU-only architectures.

papers.title: Mollification Regularization and Asymptotic Correction for Analytical Expansion of BSDEs with Non-Smooth Terminal Conditions. I. Theory
papers.authors: Liangliang Zhang
papers.abstract: The analytical expansion method for BSDEs of Zhang (2017) breaks down when the terminal condition psi has kinks or discontinuities. We replace psi by psi_epsilon = psi * rho_epsilon and derive a joint error decomposition whose expansion constants explicitly track the derivative blow-up as epsilon tends to 0. For symmetric mollifiers the leading weak bias cancels. The associated balanced rates are conditional on an explicitly stated uniform local-to-global Taylor-propagation assumption: under that assumption the benchmark (l, m, alpha) = (0, 2, 1) gives epsilon* ~ delta_t^{1/3} and weak rate 2/3. Without it, the rigorous additive bound gives no decay when m - 2l = 2; an unconditional positive rate is obtained only for m - 2l > 2. Asymptotic corrections cancel the weak bias through order epsilon^{2J}; their faster exponents are formal targets unless the auxiliary expansion errors and the Picard defect satisfy additional rate conditions, which we state explicitly. For the driver-free fixed-center scheme we identify an n-independent terminal-representation error and show that it depends on the expansion center and on the terminal representative; change-of-basis invariance does not imply centering independence. A Gaussian moment-compression layer combines whitening, a Stein recursion, and knapsack truncation with a jet-conditioned error certificate. This Part I contains the theory, with all proofs self-contained; numerical evidence and implementation measurements are reported separately in the companion paper (Part II).

papers.title: VoxSAOR: Semantic-Aware Occupancy Robustification via Aleatoric Uncertainty Modeling
papers.authors: Mengfei Duan; Yuheng Zhang; Guoqiang Zhao; Yuanfan Zheng; Kailun Yang et al.
papers.abstract: Vision-based 3D occupancy prediction provides a dense semantic representation of scenes for autonomous driving and embodied perception, yet remains vulnerable to occlusion, depth ambiguity, and projection errors that induce spatially varying reliability in voxel features. Existing methods typically map voxel representations to semantic predictions without explicitly modeling such observation-induced feature variations. To address this limitation, we propose VoxSAOR, a semantic-aware occupancy robustification framework that models aleatoric uncertainty through feature-space proxies. It first quantifies Local Semantic Consistency (LSC) to derive a voxel-wise structural stability prior and uses cross-view semantic consensus to filter unreliable semantic correspondences. Within each semantic category, spatially matched stable and ambiguous voxels form stable-to-ambiguous feature transitions, which are modeled by a class-conditional diagonal Gaussian distribution, capturing both feature displacement and dispersion. Guided by these proxy distributions, Aleatoric Regime Ensemble Learning (AREL) trains independently parameterized prediction heads using feature perturbations at progressively increasing scales, with perturbation strength modulated by structural reliability. At inference, proxy modeling and sampling are disabled, and all heads process the same observed features; their output probabilities are then averaged to produce a deterministic consensus prediction without requiring sampling. Experiments across multiple datasets and occupancy backbones demonstrate the effectiveness of VoxSAOR in improving semantic occupancy prediction, long-tail recognition, and predictive calibration. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/VoxSAOR.

papers.title: Pointillist Maize: 3D Reconstruction of Field-Grown Maize Using RGB UAV Imagery
papers.authors: Dewi Endah Kharismawati; Toni Kazic
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional reconstruction can extend field phenotyping to individual maize organs, but thin, flexible, occluding structures and plant movement complicate reconstruction. We evaluated whether consumer-grade UAV RGB video processed with Structure from Motion and multi-view stereo could recover recognizable field-grown maize structures, and examined the effects of acquisition trajectories and frame sampling. COLMAP reconstructions preserved recognizable leaves, stems, tassel branches, ears, silks, and brace roots. For an equal-frame comparison, we reconstructed one plant from two sets of 295 frames from the same video: a single orbit sampled at 5 frames/second and three orbits at different altitudes (ribbon skirt) sampled at 2 frames/second. After ground removal, the reconstructions contained 520,601 and 375,318 points, respectively. The single orbit yielded greater point concentration within plant structures and fewer visible gaps, while the ribbon skirt yielded fewer scattered points and slightly lower proportions of isolated points. In densely planted nursery rows, visible voids occupied 17.57% of the rendered scene with one orbit at 1 frame/second, decreasing to 5.07% with additional serpentine passes and 2.68% when the original orbit was sampled at 3 frames/second. Additional observations also increased point dispersion associated with plant movement. A curlicue trajectory tested in a different field in 2024 produced distinguishable individual plants without visible duplicated structures, although substantial voids remained, mainly on the soil surface. These results demonstrate the feasibility of recovering recognizable maize organs from consumer UAV imagery and reveal trade-offs between acquisition strategies, reconstruction completeness, and point dispersion. Independent geometric validation is still needed before quantitative phenotyping.

papers.title: False Discovery Rate Control in Ordered Sequential Testing: Rejection-Count and Fallback Procedures
papers.authors: Anjana Grandhi; Wenge Guo; Ji Meng Loh; Sanat Sarkar
papers.abstract: We study false discovery rate (FDR) control for a fixed family of hypotheses tested sequentially in a prespecified order. Each decision uses only the current and preceding $p$-values, is not subsequently revised, and permits continued testing after non-rejections. We distinguish generalized fixed-sequence procedures based on preceding rejection counts from fallback-type procedures that additionally use recursively transferred testing levels. For rejection-count procedures, we study a position-dependent calibration under independence and a linear rule calibrated through null marginal distribution functions under positive left-tail dependence under the null. We clarify their connections to existing fixed-sequence and online FDR methods. The fallback construction combines the total number of preceding discoveries with level transfer along consecutive rejections, allowing thresholds to reflect the arrangement of earlier outcomes. We establish its FDR control under history-based positive regression dependence and, with a position-specific correction, under arbitrary dependence. For all four constructions, the guarantees extend to every deterministic testing time within the planned horizon. Gaussian simulations assess the effects of signal placement, dependence, and allocation weights. They demonstrate power gains over selected benchmarks while identifying the conservativeness of the arbitrary-dependence correction.

papers.title: Lift, See, Act: Hierarchical Robot Policy Pretraining with 3D Foundation Models
papers.authors: Yiyuan Ge; Changxing Ding; Ziyu Hao; Zijie Zheng; Xiangmin Xu
papers.abstract: Robot policy pretraining based on human videos is crucial for improving the policy's generalization ability. One main challenge for this task is the lack of explicit action-relevant representations in such unlabeled data. Recent works tend to estimate 3D hand motion trajectories from videos using 3D foundation models (3D FMs). However, they keep solely the sparse trajectories as supervision, ignoring the rich, fine-grained information produced during the trajectory extraction process. To address this issue, we propose LSA, a hierarchical robot policy pretraining framework that includes three phases: Lift, See, and Act. Specifically, the Lift phase elevates 2D video observations into dense 3D representations by adaptively aligning features in the policy's shallow layers with the intermediate representations extracted from multiple 3D FMs. Building upon these lifted representations, the See phase equips the policy with explicit geometric and interactive awareness through dual guidance. It introduces depth-map reconstruction to help the model comprehend 3D spatial layouts and utilizes hand region cues to explicitly supervise the encoder's attention toward task-relevant interaction hotspots. Empowered by the dense 3D representation learning and precise spatial guidance, our policy achieves robust and accurate robotic manipulation in the Act phase. Extensive experiments on diverse simulation and real-world tasks demonstrate that LSA significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches. The project page is available at: https://yiyuan00.github.io/Lift-See-Act.

papers.title: Generative AI-Driven Parametric Design Optimization Framework for Vehicle Closure Systems
papers.authors: Dongeon Lee; Yurim Lee; Jiyong Kim; Sanghyeon Kim; Sanghyun Lee et al.
papers.abstract: This study presents a generative AI-driven parametric design optimization framework integrating performance-oriented generation with editable computer-aided design (CAD) and downstream computer-aided engineering (CAE) analysis for industrial vehicle closure systems. The framework is demonstrated on an automotive tailgate assembly with complex geometry, coupled components, and competing performance and feasibility requirements. A production-oriented CATIA model is restructured into a reference-based parametric template with a 13-dimensional design representation. An automated CAD/CAE workflow generates parametric models, performs structural analysis, and constructs a database of mass, maximum displacement, and maximum von Mises stress. Gaussian process regression surrogates predict performance, while diffusion and flow matching models generate design candidates. The design problem minimizes mass and maximum displacement, with stress assessed as an engineering feasibility constraint. Performance-guided generation using surrogate guidance and performance-aware training using a performance-aware loss incorporate engineering objectives, with sensitivity to guidance scale and loss weight evaluated. Generative search is compared with NSGA-II under matched evaluation budgets using a common surrogate model. Selected Pareto-region candidates are reconstructed in CATIA and re-evaluated through native CAE; all verified candidates are successfully regenerated and analyzed. Relative to the baseline, the knee-point design reduces mass by 7.1% and maximum displacement by 29.4%, while extreme verified solutions achieve maximum reductions of 10.3% and 37.3%, respectively. The results demonstrate performance-oriented multi-objective design exploration compatible with editable industrial CAD and native engineering verification.

papers.title: Joint Antenna Positioning and Dynamic Beam Tracking for MA-Enabled Full-Duplex Secure ISAC Systems: A Flow Matching DRL Approach
papers.authors: Zhendong Li; Yujie Zhao; Jianle Ba; Zhou Su; Wen Chen
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) improves spectral efficiency but faces significant security challenges in dynamic wireless environments, where the potential eavesdropper is treated as the sensing target. This paper proposes a movable antenna (MA)-enabled full-duplex secure ISAC system that tracks the mobile eavesdropper while safeguarding both uplink and downlink transmissions. Specifically, an extended Kalman filter (EKF) is employed to recursively estimate and predict the eavesdropper's state from radar echoes. Building on the estimated target state, we formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the sum of the uplink and downlink secrecy rates by jointly optimizing the transmit and receive MA positions, uplink and downlink beamforming, artificial noise, and uplink transmit power. The resulting problem is challenging due to its inherent nonconvexity, strong coupling among optimization variables, and time-varying nature. Conventional iterative optimization methods may incur prohibitive computational overhead in dynamic environments, whereas existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods based on unimodal Gaussian or deterministic policies may struggle to capture complex multimodal high-reward action distributions. To address these challenges, we develop a flow matching-based deep reinforcement learning (FMDRL) algorithm for sequential joint decision-making. The proposed algorithm integrates a conditional velocity-field actor with twin critics, generating continuous actions through finite-step Euler integration and employing a deterministic decoder to enforce physical constraints on antenna positions, transmit power, and positive semidefiniteness. Extensive numerical simulations confirm that the proposed FMDRL algorithm achieves superior performance in terms of both communication security and target tracking capabilities.

papers.title: UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge 2026: Site-Calibrated Synthetic Data and Multi-Detector Fusion for Roadside 3D Detection
papers.authors: Arnav Kumar; Brijesh Soni
papers.abstract: This report summarizes the work submitted by team arnav007 (submission ID 1054222) for the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge (V2X-Real track) at the IEEE BigData Cup 2026. The primary objective is to train 3D detectors for vehicles, pedestrians, and trucks using only synthetic roadside LiDAR data, and to generate synthetic scans that are realistic enough to be indistinguishable from real ones. A CARLA based pipeline is developed and calibrated to the fixed sensor site, accurately modeling the range image, including no-return beams, based on unlabelled real development scans. A combined inference detector, using multiple 3D detectors (VoxelNeXt, PV-RCNN, and SECOND) trained exclusively on synthetic data, is also proposed. Each scan is aligned to the synthetic ground plane and processed through the detectors at multiple ground heights. The resulting bounding boxes are fused using bird's-eye view (BEV) clustering, followed by class-specific post-processing to refine heading, box size, and filter low-confidence detections. The final submission achieved a combined score of 0.8947. The ablation study shows that per-scan ground leveling more than doubled the real-scan mAP, while fusing boxes across different heights and models further improved performance.

papers.title: InterRSGaussian: Interactive Multi-view Instance Segmentation for 3D Remote Sensing Scenes
papers.authors: Zipeng Qi; Zhengxia Zou; Zhenwei Shi
papers.abstract: Remote sensing image segmentation plays a critical role in various applications. Interactive instance segmentation, a specialized task within image segmentation, aims to generate precise segmentation results for target objects based on user input prompts. However, previous studies on interactive instance segmentation primarily focus on single-view images, limiting their ability to comprehensively understand complex 3D remote sensing scenes. In this study, we extend interactive instance segmentation from a single-view to a multi-view framework, which can also be easily converted to a 3D segmentation format, thus achieving more accurate and comprehensive 3D remote sensing scene perception across multiple views. First, we construct a multi-view interactive instance segmentation dataset for remote sensing, comprising five distinct scenes, each captured from about one hundred different views. Second, we propose InterRSGaussian, a novel instance segmentation method based on 3D Gaussians. InterRSGaussian enables users to provide point clicks on target objects from any arbitrary view and generates view-consistent instance segmentation results across all input views without requiring manual annotations. The resulting multi-view segmentation can further be projected onto 3D point clouds for 3D segmentation. To improve training efficiency and segmentation performance, we introduce a prior distillation network for initialization. Overall, this study extends traditional 2D remote sensing scene perception into a 3D multi-view framework, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of target objects in complex environments with user interactivity.

papers.title: Training-Free Anonymization of Driving Data with Promptable Segmentation and 3D Human Mesh Recovery
papers.authors: Max A. Buettner; Mark Azer; Fabian B. Flohr
papers.abstract: Camera recordings for autonomous driving contain faces and license plates that should be anonymized before labeling, sharing, or training. Dedicated detectors can miss small plates and faces behind vehicle glass. We present FM-Anonymize, a training-free anonymization pipeline that combines promptable segmentation, 3D human mesh recovery, and generative replacement. SAM 3 locates people, faces, and vehicles and searches zoomed vehicle crops for plates, occupants, and windows. SAM 3D Body assesses face visibility from head orientation and projects head regions for blurring. Optional diffusion inpainting replaces eligible blurred heads with synthetic faces, guided by estimated pose and keypoints. On PP4AV, the blur pipeline protects 97.8% of faces and 95.5% of plates, the highest privacy recall of all compared methods at their default settings. On our recordings, where the localization thresholds were set, it protects 97.1% of faces and 93.4% of plates, compared with 93.7%/73.0% for UrbanAnonymizer, 42.7%/40.7% for EgoBlur, and 96.6% of faces for deface. Synthetic replacement raises full-body keypoint average precision over blurring from 54.1% to 79.6% on our recordings and from 39.9% to 68.3% on PP4AV. Code and configurations are available on https://github.com/max-a-ai/FM-Anonymize

papers.title: Interlocking Tiling of 3D Finite Domains
papers.authors: Xuyang Ma; Rulin Chen; Chaewoon Kim; Ying He; Peng Song
papers.abstract: A K-hedral tiling of a 3D finite domain is a covering of the domain with tiles without gaps or overlaps, where each tile is congruent to one of the K distinct shapes called prototiles. To use 3D K-hedral tilings in practice, they need to satisfy two requirements. First, K should be small to reduce the fabrication cost (e.g., through reusable molds) and simplify the (dis)assembly process. Second, a K-hedral tiling result should be structurally stable, in particular via interlocking, where all the tiles are immobilized by their geometric arrangement, except the key. Since these two requirements are often in conflict, existing approaches always trade one for the other.   In this work, we formulate a new tiling problem called interlocking tiling, aiming to generate 3D K-hedral tilings that satisfy the above two requirements simultaneously. Given a 3D finite domain represented as a voxel grid, our goal is to compute a small prototile set whose instances exactly tile the input domain while ensuring that the tiling result forms an interlocking assembly. To solve this challenging problem, we propose a twolevel computational approach that hierarchically decomposes the input domain into interlocking parts (domain-level partitioning) and further partitions each part into interlocking tiles (part-level partitioning). To guide the part-level partitioning, we propose a new graph representation with regular structures to facilitate the generation of tiles with identical shapes while ensuring that they are interlocking. Our approach allows generating interlocking tilings that exactly cover 3D finite domains with diverse shapes while achieving high prototile reuse. We compared our approach with state-of-the-art methods to demonstrate its superiority, and validated the practicality of our interlocking tiling results via fabricating two of them.

papers.title: Phase-conjugate Gaussian encoding for continuous-variable quantum key distribution with a single phase-sensitive amplifier
papers.authors: Zhenlin Zhao; Dawei Wang
papers.abstract: Phase-conjugate encoding is naturally compatible with shared phase-sensitive amplification and joint detection, offering a compact optical receiver architecture for continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD). Here, we develop a unified encoding and security framework for two-mode Gaussian CVQKD with tunable phase-conjugate intermode correlations matched to a joint receiver comprising a single phase-sensitive amplifier (PSA) and one balanced photodetector. We present both coherent-state and squeezed-state prepare-and-measure protocols that use the same transmitted ensemble. The two preparations can be implemented through classically precoded Gaussian displacements of coherent sidebands or a directly generated two-mode squeezed vacuum, respectively, without an actual optical mode converter. The encoding and detection scheme separates low-variance joint quadratures for key generation from high-variance joint quadratures carrying private random modulation. This complementary modulation can reduce Eve's Holevo information without changing the Alice--Bob mutual information. Numerical results show that optimized correlated coherent-state encoding achieves higher asymptotic key rates at long distances and extends the positive-key range compared with optimized single-mode coherent-state modulation. The optimal intermode correlation increases with transmission distance, and the range advantage persists under the symmetric correlated two-mode Gaussian attacks considered here. These results provide a theoretical basis for the design and implementation of PSA-enhanced two-mode CVQKD with phase-conjugate encoding.

papers.title: HoloGene: Learning to Lift Sliced Spatial Transcriptomics to Holistic 3D Gene Fields
papers.authors: Yumin Zheng; Qingtian Zhu; Ziyan Zhu; Kailu Song; Yinqiang Zheng et al.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) provides spatially resolved gene expression measurements, but most 3D ST datasets are acquired as independently processed 2D sections. Computational approaches span slice registration and integration, explicit or generative interpolation, and coordinate-field modeling. Within the last family, implicit neural representations (INRs) offer a continuous, coordinate-queryable parameterization, but standard isotropic coordinate encodings do not explicitly reflect that serial-section measurements are dense in-plane and sparse along the axial direction. We present HoloGene, an anisotropic conditional INR framework for estimating continuous 3D gene-expression fields from pre-registered ST sections. Its central contribution is an acquisition-aware factorization that couples dense in-plane synthesis with sparse axial evolution using established GAE, FiLM, pseudo-label supervision, and CORAL components. HoloGene compresses high-dimensional expression profiles into a graph-autoencoder latent manifold, uses pseudo-label-derived signature conditioning to provide coarse intra-section context, and applies depth-dependent FiLM modulation to model axial variation. A signature-stratified correlation-alignment regularizer encourages cross-slice covariance alignment in latent features. Using held-out measured sections as cross-sectional references, HoloGene improves reconstruction accuracy and biological preservation metrics compared with general-purpose INRs and adapted spatial-transcriptomics baselines. These results support anisotropic conditional modeling as a practical strategy for estimating 3D expression fields from discontinuous ST sections. Code is available at https://github.com/Szym29/HoloGene.

papers.title: Structure-Guided Multi-Granularity Spatiotemporal Transformer for Efficient Monocular 3D Human Pose Estimation
papers.authors: Sheng Xu; Aoduo Li; Rongli He
papers.abstract: Existing multi-granularity methods for monocular 3D human pose estimation emphasize spatial joint features while underusing skeletal structure, including global connectivity and temporal continuity. Moreover, modeling entire frame sequences incurs high computational costs. We propose a Structure-Aware Multi-Granularity Spatiotemporal Transformer that integrates structural priors across spatial and temporal representations for accurate and efficient pose estimation. A three-level feature extractor captures human topology at the joint, bone, and limb levels. Gated Adaptive Spatial Attention (GASA) embeds structural constraints into spatial attention, while Multi-Granularity Feature Enhancement (MGFE) uses hierarchical pooling and fusion to strengthen local details and global semantics. Temporal Segment Fusion (TSF) aligns temporal contexts across granularities to capture both short- and long-range motion patterns. Hierarchical Cross-Attention (HCA) promotes spatiotemporal interaction between granularities, and Keyframe Attention (KFA) selects informative motion segments to reduce redundancy and computational cost. Experiments demonstrate improved accuracy and efficiency over conventional Transformer-based approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of structure-aware multi-granularity modeling for monocular 3D human pose estimation.

papers.title: EPI-SST: Renewal-Structured State-Space Transformers for Epidemic Forecasting
papers.authors: Yiyun Chen; Zewen Liu; Shengpu Tang; Max S. Y. Lau; Wei Jin
papers.abstract: Epidemic forecasting supports public health decisions ranging from capacity planning to intervention timing, for which both point accuracy and calibrated uncertainty are essential. Although neural models have advanced point forecasting, producing reliable probabilistic predictions over multiple future horizons remains challenging. Renewal models encode epidemic propagation, while neural forecasters learn flexible multi-horizon representations; integrating these strengths within a probabilistic future rollout remains underexplored. We propose EPI-SST (Epidemic State Space Transformer), a probabilistic forecaster centered on an evidence-driven renewal transition. At each horizon, neural evidence produces a bounded update to an internal multiplier and advances a finite-memory renewal state that generates the future mean trajectory. A separate heteroscedastic Gaussian head controls predictive scale using a validation-selected log-variance penalty. Across four epidemic surveillance benchmarks, EPI-SST achieves the lowest pooled RMSE on every dataset, reducing RMSE by up to 14.2 percent relative to the strongest baseline. It also achieves the lowest continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) at horizons h = 4, 5, 6 on every dataset, with reductions of up to 43 percent relative to the strongest probabilistic baseline. During the abnormal 2019-2020 influenza season, EPI-SST reduces CRPS by 16.9 percent and calibration error by 78.9 percent; a three-seed replication preserves its distributional lead. Ablation studies and frozen-path interventions show that the renewal transition, attention conditioning, horizon coupling, and uncertainty-scale control make complementary contributions to predictive performance.

papers.title: Maximum Scores and Treatment Feedback in Regression Discontinuity Designs
papers.authors: Subir Hait
papers.abstract: Hospitals use repeated risk scores to decide when to send an alert. Some evaluations summarize these scores by their maximum and use the maximum as the running variable in a regression discontinuity (RD) design. The maximum shows correctly whether a patient was ever alerted. However, it can include scores recorded after an earlier alert has already changed care. In this paper, we study what the maximum-score RD estimates when an earlier intervention changes a later score. We use a two-assessment model and derive a formula that splits the RD contrast into the causal effect and a composition term. When feedback moves scores in one direction, the composition term equals the relative jump in the density of the maximum at the cutoff times a prognostic contrast. Therefore, an exactly continuous density means no bias, and the population density jump bounds the bias. Valid inference on the jump turns this into a confidence bound under a stated sensitivity assumption. Within this model, bias behind a continuous density requires feedback in both directions. For this case, we bound bias by total boundary movement and construct conservative confidence sets for binary outcomes under explicit sensitivity and smoothness assumptions. We give closed forms for independent uniform scores and for correlated Gaussian scores. In one example, a true risk reduction of four percentage points appears as a one-point increase. Simulations confirm the formulas. Narrower bandwidths, robust bias correction, and machine-learning covariate adjustment do not remove the bias. A fuzzy RD on the first score recovers the causal effect when early and late treatment have the same effect. Our results concern how the running variable is built. We do not assess any published clinical study.

papers.title: NF-VLA: A Normalizing-Flow Baseline for Vision-Language-Action Learning
papers.authors: Ruichen Deng; Qinyu Zhao; Yong-Hyun Park; Mutian Tong; Liang Zheng et al.
papers.abstract: Autoregressive normalizing flows (NFs) provide a tractable density for learning and sampling continuous robot actions. We show that a single maximum-likelihood objective can train vision--language--action (VLA) policies competitive with leading methods on manipulation benchmarks. We present NF-VLA, which combines conditional autoregressive normalizing flows with score-based action refinement. Its deep--shallow architecture concentrates visual, language, and proprioceptive prefix conditioning in a high-capacity deep block, while unconditioned shallow blocks provide a shared invertible action transformation. The vision--language backbone and flow are jointly trained by exact maximum likelihood on Gaussian-smoothed action chunks. The same learned density supplies a single score-based correction at inference, refining generated actions to account for training-time smoothing without a separately trained denoiser. Trained on LIBERO from a pretrained vision--language backbone without robot pretraining, NF-VLA achieves 98.35\% success across the four standard suites and 72.6\% on LIBERO-Plus using the same checkpoint without further fine-tuning. Ablations show that deep-only prefix conditioning and score-based refinement both improve closed-loop success. Together, these results establish carefully structured autoregressive flows as a competitive approach to VLA control, with one learned density supporting policy training, action generation, and refinement.

papers.title: PoCoAttn: Position-Content Collaborative Sparse Attention for Fast and High-Fidelity Video Generation
papers.authors: Jianwen Wu; Meiling Wang; Junkang Zhou; Yipeng Shen; Haoran You
papers.abstract: Video diffusion transformers rely on 3D full attention over tens of thousands of spatiotemporal tokens, and its quadratic cost dominates inference latency. Sparse attention reduces this cost, but existing methods face a dilemma: static methods apply predefined masks and cannot capture input-dependent attention, whereas dynamic methods reconstruct the sparse mask repeatedly, paying online to rediscover positional structure that is largely stable across inputs. To this end, we propose PoCoAttn, a training-free sparse attention framework that separates input-stable from input-dependent attention and resolves the former offline and the latter online. PoCoAttn features: (1) A relative-offset analysis of 3D query-key pairs, which shows that video attention decomposes into an input-stable positional prior that carries most of the attention mass and a small content-dependent residual. (2) A position-content collaborative sparse attention mechanism, which retrieves positional keys from offline-calibrated tables, selects content keys online with a head-adaptive ratio between the two sources, and compensates for the discarded keys to approximate full attention. (3) A step-adaptive budget allocation algorithm, which models how early-step sparse attention errors are amplified along the denoising trajectory and derives the optimal sparsity budget per step. Extensive experiments across four video diffusion models and three tasks show that PoCoAttn consistently achieves a better speed-fidelity Pareto frontier than state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, improving PSNR by 1.9 to 5.0 dB over baselines and delivering up to 4.1$\times$ attention and 2.0$\times$ denoising speedups over dense FlashAttention-3 attention.

papers.title: Population structure of the velocity distribution in normal shock waves: Gaussian representations, Mach-number similarity, and prediction
papers.authors: Ehsan Roohi
papers.abstract: Normal shock waves are commonly described as mixtures of upstream and downstream Maxwellians. Discrete-velocity solutions of three relaxation models up to Mach 12 and direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) of hard-sphere and variable-hard-sphere gases up to Mach 25 are used to examine the population structure, Mach-number similarity and upstream precursor of their velocity distributions. Three anisotropic Gaussian populations reproduce the streamwise reduced distributions of the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) model and of DSMC to within 4\% up to Mach 12, and of DSMC to within 6\% at Mach 25, whereas two Maxwellians incur errors up to 50\% (BGK) and 37\% (DSMC). Collision histories identify the hard-sphere beam with unscattered stream molecules, which carry half of the peak viscous stress; the other populations are effective descriptions, not collision classes. Above Mach 5, Rankine--Hugoniot-scaled distributions are nearly Mach-independent, with corrections linear in $1/M^2$, consistent with the scaled kinetic equation. At equal normalised density, Mach 8 and 12 give the heat flux and stress at Mach 25 within 1\%, comparable to the accuracy of the reference; with one moment equation for position, physical-space profiles follow within 5\%. Comparing three prediction methods shows that the accuracy comes from the scaling; the Gaussian form adds compactness. Ahead of the shock, the mass of upstream-moving molecules decays as a stretched exponential with effective exponent 0.68--0.87. Collisions regenerate upstream-moving molecules, which explains a decay slower than free-flight survival; a linear cascade model with a downstream-Maxwellian source and no input from the shock interior reproduces the decay rates within 1.2\%.

papers.title: Maximum likelihood degrees of 3D polytopes built from polygons of ML degree one
papers.authors: Eliana Duarte; Federico Lazzeri; Bowen Li; Ludovico Piazza; Bernhard Reinke et al.
papers.abstract: We construct 3D polytopes that admit a scaling with maximum likelihood (ML) degree one by using codimension zero toric fiber products of lower-dimensional polytopes and classify all the 3D polytopes that can be constructed in this way. We also study a family of 3D polytopes whose faces admit ML degree one scalings. We give a tight lower bound for the ML degree of these polytopes with a square base and we show that every value between this bound and the normalized volume of the polytope can be attained. These values depend on counting common and repeated roots associated to certain univariate polynomials. This is similar in spirit to the description of the possible ML degrees of rational normal scrolls.

papers.title: CiGS: Conduction in Gaussian Splats for Interior Temperature Field from Thermal Images
papers.authors: Liu Zhenyuan; Bharath Seshadri; Bailey Miller; George Kopanas; Ionnais Gkioulekas et al.
papers.abstract: We present a method for inferring the interior temperature distribution of a solid object from registered multi-view visible-spectrum and thermal images, even when the thermal views cover only part of its surface. We formulate steady-state heat conduction as a Laplace boundary value problem and solve it with a direct boundary integral equation discretized over a point cloud: a Gaussian reconstruction of the visible-spectrum images supplies the boundary geometry, and the thermal images supply the boundary data. We do not build surface or volume meshes at any stage in our method. Instead, we sample collocation points from rendered depth without the pixels at depth discontinuities, and use a density subtraction that keeps the interior evaluation accurate up to the surface. The whole chain is differentiable, and we use it to recover the pose and depth of heating pipes, insulation defects, and the shape of cracks from thermal images. We validate our method through experiments on boundary value problems with Dirichlet-only and mixed Dirichlet and Robin boundaries, using synthetic and real captured data on scenes with challenging topology. These experiments show that our method matches analytical solutions and has better accuracy than FEM solvers.

papers.title: From XR Sketches to CAD: Preserving Design Intent with AI
papers.authors: Trudi Di Qi
papers.abstract: Extended reality (XR) allows designers to sketch shapes directly in 3D, but converting these sketches into editable, feature-based CAD requires interpreting their intent. A sketch may contain drawing errors, intended features, and design choices that remain open. Correcting every irregularity risks erasing intended features, while automatic completion may impose choices the designer has not made. We argue that AI should add precision without overriding design intent, considering both the resulting shape and how the CAD model behaves during later edits. To guide this process, we propose a conceptual framework that distinguishes errors from intentions in individual sketch properties and relates them to correction, preservation, and exploration in editable CAD. We also outline five research directions for sketch interpretation, CAD construction, and evaluation, with testable hypotheses for selected questions.

papers.title: Achievable Information Rate for FTN under a Reduced Complexity BCJR Receiver
papers.authors: Zichao Zhang; Gokhan M. Guvensen; Melda Yuksel; Halim Yanikomeroglu
papers.abstract: The capacity of faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling in additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels has been established and is achieved by Gaussian inputs. However, the capacity of FTN signaling with finite-constellations is not yet fully characterized. The achievable information rate (AIR) provides a lower bound on this constrained capacity by quantifying the rate supported by a specified input distribution and receiver. This paper investigates the AIR of FTN signaling with finite constellations using full-state and reduced-state Bahl-Cocke-Jelinek-Raviv (BCJR) receivers, with bidirectional decision feedback incorporated into the reduced-state receiver. Especially, the detection problem is formulated in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), where a geometric foundation is established to understand FTN under severe time packing. The formulation establishes that the Ungerboeck metric remains valid even when the noise covariance is singular. We further characterize detection errors geometrically using RKHS distances between competing sequences. We also study outage probability for reduced-state detection, which occurs when AIR is zero, in addition to deriving the zero-AIR outage criterion for reduced-state detection. Unlike ISI-free Nyquist signaling, reduced-state FTN detection can retain residual ISI that causes the receiver to assign excessive confidence to incorrect symbols, leading to outage even at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Our results confirm both the spectral efficiency gains and the feasibility of FTN systems employing finite constellations and realistic receiver architectures.
